pride_data.title: Characterization of the N- and C-terminal domain interface of the three main apoE isoforms
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to investigate the conformations of the apolipoprotein isoforms apoE2, apoE3, and apoE4. Cross-linking data was generated using the reagents disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS), pimelic dihydrazide (PDH), and 4-(4,6-Dimethoxy-1,3,5-triazin-2-yl)-4-methylmorpholinium (DMTMM) chloride. Intramolecular interactions derived from the cross-linking experiments were combined with molecular modeling approaches.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Cross-linking was performed according to previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014; Mohammadi et al., Anal. Chem., 2021). Cross-linked proteins were (1) digested in solution using endoproteinase Lys-C and trypsin and fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography, or (2) digested in gel with trypsin after electrophoretic separation. LC-MS/MS analysis was performed on Orbitrap Elite and LTQ Orbitrap XL mass spectrometers.  Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest/xProphet (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequences of the target apoE and shuffled decoy sequences. Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 0.2 Da for “common”-type fragment ions and 0.3 Da for “xlink”-type fragment ions. The false discovery rate was set to 5% at the level of non-redundant cross-link peptide pairs using xProphet. Label-free quantification was performed using xTract (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2014). All identifications are provided in two spreadsheet files for the in-solution and in-gel digests, respectively. A spreadsheet file that provides experimental details for all raw files is also provided. Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; pdh; dmtmm; apolipoprotein e; apoe
